'''Usarufa''' is a [[Kainantu language]] spoken by the people of the same name in [[Papua New Guinea]]. It belongs to the Gauwa branch of the Kainantu family of the [[Kainantu–Goroka languages]].  The language area consists of six villages: Moife, Imikori, Irafo, Kagu, Agura 1, and Agura 2.  Its [[ISO 639]] code is ''usa''.

As of 2009, the language was reported to have had about 1200 speakers and no fluent speakers below the age of 25, which makes it an [[endangered language]].

The distribution of these consonants is determined by their position within a stress group, a segment which has one primary [[Stress (linguistics)|stress]], the placement of which is determined by a [[Pitch-accent language|pitch contour]]. This stress group may consist of two or more [[syllable]]s. Only {{IPA|/p t k m n w j/}} can occur as the onset of a stress group, and only {{IPA|/ʔ/}} can occur finally. In stress-medial position all consonant phonemes can occur, and {{IPA|/p k/}} are realised as {{IPAblink|β}} and {{IPAblink|ɣ}}, respectively. {{IPA|/ɾ/}} may be realised as {{IPAblink|ɺ}}.
